fixes.explanation: Nobody's packing Leah's bags, friend. Verse 31 says, “When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb…” He saw her first, and then He acted. I think that's the part worth holding onto.

Not this time, baker. The very next line says, “Then Leah stopped having children.” Judah makes four sons, and then the baby parade stops. I think it's a lovely place to pause, since Leah names him with “This time I will praise the LORD.”

You got it, baker. After Judah, the text says, “Then Leah stopped having children.” Four sons, and the baby parade takes a break. Her last words at that birth were “This time I will praise the LORD,” and I think that's a good note to stop on.

No borrowing needed, friend. Bilhah is Rachel's servant, and Leah has a servant of her own. Verse 9 says Leah saw she had stopped having children, so she gave Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. Leah handles this one on her own.

Leah waving Jacob off toward Rachel? Not in this verse, baker. Genesis 30:9 says she saw that she had stopped having children, so she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. I think Leah isn't ready to sit this one out.
Foolish? Leah isn't having a foolish day, friend. She says, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” Then she names her son Asher. Somebody give that woman a moment to enjoy it.

You got it, friend. Reuben finds mandrakes in the field during the wheat harvest and brings them to his mother, Leah. Rachel, his aunt, doesn't get them delivered. She has to ask, and she begs Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”
